rules.title: Finite-dimensional vector-space convention

origin.tex:
From now on we will study only finite-dimensional vector spaces.
In the rest of this book we shall take `vector space' to mean 
`finite-dimensional vector space'.

rules.application: Carry the author's convention with material after this source passage; do not rewrite local hypotheses or apply it to earlier text. A source convention is not a claim that every object in a fragment is a vector space.

rules.title: Original homogeneous-coordinate and affine-chart definitions

editorial_notes.text: Division by c and the representative with third coordinate 1 apply only when c is nonzero. A nonzero vector with c=0 represents a projective point at infinity and has no representative on z=1. The origin of the affine screen is (0,0,1), not the excluded zero homogeneous vector.

rules.title: Original affine and projective transformation displays

editorial_notes.text: An invertible projective transformation is represented by a nonsingular 3-by-3 matrix up to nonzero scale. Writing its bottom-right entry as 1 assumes that entry is nonzero; an invertible matrix with bottom-right entry 0 cannot be scaled to the displayed form. General affine maps may be singular; an affine automorphism instead requires an invertible 2-by-2 linear block. The printed matrices are unchanged.

rules.application: Retain the printed matrices and separately state nonsingularity and the nonzero bottom-right normalization limit; do not infer that every projective transformation has this representative. In the last supplied answer, the z-axis matrix has a zero third row and the y-axis matrix has a zero second row. They erase the coordinate on the purported fixed axis, so neither is a rotation; even at theta=0 they are not the identity. The fixed-axis diagonal entries must be 1: entry (3,3) in the first matrix and (2,2) in the second. All other printed coefficients, including the y-rotation sign convention, are retained. This note does not replace the printed source.
